# Episode Recap

The episode 1 featured:

- The **shed now having a tunnel** built in which led not quite to Narnia, but **to a Greek themed gazebo.**
    - Whether this is a permanent area, or a temporary area that only featured in the golden apple task is unknown. Time will tell!
- For the second series in a row, the **teams were introduced in this premiere episode for the series.** The teams are:
    - Isy Suttie and Nina Conti.
    - CHloe Petts, Matt Lucas and Richard Ayoade.
- The introduction of the teams in Episode 1 is always a surprise since we typically have yet to fully digest each contestant as an individual. It worked a treat in Series 21 though; _He's so famous!_
- The **teams themselves are quite the surprise**, and no doubt due to availability and scheduling. 
    - The **main surprise comes from assigning Chloe and Richard to the same team**. Prior to the episode, I suspected with relatively low probability, that they would be on the same team.
    - Ultimately, it shows how little I know in how the Taskmaster universe works.
    - I am **excited by the team of Isy and Nina**; it is almost like a mumsy night out. I did feel that they were at a significant disadvantage during the team task; disassembling and reassembling a bed is easier with more people!
- This episode featured the musical talents of our contestants through the _"Sing a passionate duet to yourself."_, and showcased that this a **very** musical cast.
    - All contestants attempts featured them playing their instruments to a reasonably competent degree. Only Nina was the one who showed some real hesistation and stage fright; she was making up the lyrics to her song as she went along though.
- **Richard Ayoade has already delievered his awkward, disruptive humour.** 
    - I suspect that this will continue throughout the series, and what fans are expecting from him and the show.
    - It was slightly disappointing that his we was _extremely_ low effort and energy in the live studio task. I know that this is his style of comedy, but he could try at least bit harder and show some respect for the Taskmaster!



```{r ep-performance-grade, fig.cap = "Episode 1 Performance Report Cards", fig.topcap = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
sys.source(file.path(perform_dir, "ep_performance_table.R"), envir = multiverse_env)
multiverse_env$ep_grade_perf_table
```

:::{.insights}
- We saw **Chloe Petts be crowned the winner of Episode 1! She accumulated 19 points.**
- However, Chloe cannot be too comfortable with her episode win, **Nina Conti and Matt Lucas were hot on here heels with 18 and 17 points respectively.** 
- **Isy and Richard rounded out the episodes placements, both achieving 13 points and being tied in 4th place.**
    - These are certainly not the lowest scores for placing last in an episode. However, the disqualification in the first pre-recorded task (_"Find the golden apple and place it on the golden plate"_) certainly did not help with their episode performance.
    - Richard was also lucky that his win in the live studio task made him joint 4th, rather than placing 5th. I was quite surprised that he won this task despite the low effort and energy he was exuding. But I guess he really liked those belts...
    
:::

# Gamble's Gamble

## Within-Episode Ranking Distributions

```{r ep-rankings, fig.cap = "Within Episode Ranking Distribution: Using Data up to Episode 1 ", out.width = "49%", fig.show="hold", cache = FALSE}
graph_dir <- here("static", "code", "R", "graphs")
multiverse_env$remain_num_eps <- multiverse_env$num_eps_series - multiverse_env$sim_max_episode_used


sys.source(file.path(graph_dir, "ep_ranking_distribution.R"), envir = multiverse_env)

multiverse_env$ep_ranking_dist_plot
```

:::{.insights}
Based on the the task attempts of Episode 1 only, Figure \@ref(fig:ep-rankings) has the estimated distributions for each contestants placement in an episode:

- These distributions are unsurprisingly peaked on each contestants placement in episode 1 (roughly).
- The most probable ranking in an episode for each contestant are:
    - Chloe: 1st with 63.37% probability.
    - Isy: 5th with 49.84% chance.
    - Matt: 2nd with 35.55%.
    - Nina: 2nd with 31.65%.
    - Richard: 5th with 37.48%.
- We also see that each contestant does have a non-zero chance of winning an episode.
    - After Chloe, Nina is the next most likely to win an episode (31.59%), then Matt (19.09%), then Richard (6.05%), and then Isy (0.84%).
- **However, ** we do expect these distributions to change as we see more task attempts from each episode. 
:::

## End-of-Series Ranking Distributions
```{r series-rankings, fig.cap = "Series Ranking Distribution: Using Data up to Episode 1.", out.width = "49%", fig.show='hold', cache = FALSE}

sys.source(file.path(graph_dir, "series_ranking_distribution.R"), envir = multiverse_env)

multiverse_env$series_ranking_dist_plot
```

:::{.insights}
We also have our first estimates for end of series ranking distributions (see Figure \@ref(fig:series-rankings)):

- These **end of series ranking distributions are very much aligned with the outcome of Episode 1**; they are peaked and centered on their ranking at the end of Episode 1:
- The most probable series outcome for each contestant are:
    - Chloe: 1st with 92.18% probability.
    - Isy: 5th with 71.85% chance.
    - Matt: 3rd with 75.01%.
    - Nina: 2nd with 70.16%.
    - Richard: 4th with 73.97%.
- From these distributions, the main uncertainty seems to arise as to who will place 2nd and 3rd (Nina or Matt), and 4th and 5th (Richard or Isy). 
- **Again, ** we do expect these distributions to change as we see more task attempts from each episode. 
:::

## Joint Cast Ranking Distributions
```{r joint-cast-ranking, fig.cap = "Joint Distribution of Cast Series Ranking: Using Data up to Episode 1.", out.width = "49%", fig.show='hold', cache = FALSE}
assign("prev_ep_joint_pred", c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0), envir = multiverse_env) # To pass on a previous prediction
sys.source(file.path(graph_dir, "joint_cast_ranking_distribution.R"), envir = multiverse_env)

multiverse_env$joint_cast_ranking_dist_plot
```

:::{.insights}
The most probable outcome for the entire cast at the end of the series is:

- 1st: Chloe Petts
- 2nd: Nina Conti
- 3rd: Matt Lucas
- 4th: Richard Ayoade
- 5th: Isy Suttie

This is **estimated to occur with 47.24% probability**. This prediction is aligned with the outcome of Episode 1 minus the tie in 4th place.

There only 2 other outcomes which have more than 10% chance of occurring. These vary on who will end up in 4th and 5th place (Isy or Richard), and 2nd and 3rd place (Matt or Nina).
:::

# What Have We Learnt Today?

:::{.infobox .today}
We've learnt that:

- Daddy's Back! Series 22 of UK Taskmaster has got off to a fine start.
- **Chloe Petts won the first episode of the series with 19 points.** However, Nina and Matt could have easily claimed this title if the live studio task panned out slightly differently.
- We also saw the **teams for this series being established in this debut episode**. The **teams are `[Nina, Isy]` and `[Chloe, Matt, Richard]`**.
- This is **an extremely musically capable cast!** They all appear to play musical instruments to a reasonable standard. 
- Richard Ayoade is already satisfying his awkward, disruptive quota. 
- Currently, **our prediction of how the series will pan out after 10 episode is `[1st: Chloe, 2nd: Nina, 3rd: Matt, 4th: Richard, 5th: Isy]` with 47.24% probability**. 
- We expect our distributions, predictions and inferences to change as the series progresses, even substantially at times!
    - In fact, we even expect the distributions to be quite volatile (changing a lot) in the first half of the series, from episode to episode, due to limited data (task attempts available). 
    - They may even be inaccurate in the first half of the series!
